name: Hypobetalipoproteinemia

criteria.description: Persistently low plasma LDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein B levels
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the APOB gene
Family history of low LDL cholesterol consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Presence of clinical features such as fatty liver or neurological symptoms in homozygous or compound heterozygous cases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistently low LDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein B levels plus identification of pathogenic APOB gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Heterozygous individuals may be asymptomatic; homozygous or compound heterozygous cases present more severe clinical features.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Markedly reduced plasma LDL cholesterol concentration
searchTerms: very low LDL cholesterol in blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with low LDL-C in family members
searchTerms: family history of low LDL cholesterol
inherited pattern of low bad cholesterol

common.symptomName: Mild neurological symptoms including ataxia or peripheral neuropathy (in homozygous cases)
Fat malabsorption or steatorrhea (in severe cases)
searchTerms: fatty stools due to poor fat absorption

occasional.symptomName: Retinitis pigmentosa or other retinal abnormalities

searchTerms: nerve problems from vitamin E lack
balance and coordination issues due to vitamin E
nerve dysfunction from low vitamin E

rare.symptomName: Coagulopathy due to vitamin K deficiency
searchTerms: bleeding problems from vitamin K lack
blood clotting issues due to vitamin deficiency
coagulopathy linked to vitamin K shortage

rare.symptomName: Severe fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K)
searchTerms: lack of vitamins A, D, E, K
deficiency of vitamins important for bones and nerves

laboratory: Markedly reduced LDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein B levels
Low fat-soluble vitamin levels (especially vitamin E)
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing hepatic steatosis
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in APOB gene detected by molecular genetic testing
other: Family pedigree consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Low HDL cholesterol instead of LDL

redFlags: Progressive neurological symptoms such as ataxia or peripheral neuropathy
Signs of fat-soluble vitamin deficiency (e.g., vision loss, coagulopathy)
references: Hussain MM. Familial hypobetalipoproteinemia: genetics and clinical spectrum. Curr Opin Lipidol. 2000;11(2):147-52.
Pullinger CR, et al. Familial hypobetalipoproteinemia: molecular basis and clinical implications. J Lipid Res. 2008;49(6):1156-66.
